Early lecturers rarely agreed on how memory works, and one tutor argued that the mind keeps few items at once.
Later work supported her view.
Her students found the claim bold.
Practice should be spread over several days.
which is why cramming fails for most learners.
Take vitamin C.
The body needs it.
J. K. Rowan wrote this.
Barlow, T. M. disagreed.
Participants studied word lists in quiet rooms and returned a week later for a recall test.
Those who tested themselves between sessions recalled more words than those who only reread.
The pattern held for every list length that the team tried, from ten words up to sixty.
Short lists were remembered well by everyone, so the gap between the groups was small there.
Long lists showed the largest benefit, because rereading alone left most of the words unfamiliar.
Volunteers also rated how confident they felt, and those ratings did not track the real scores closely.
Many of them guessed that rereading had helped more than it did.
The team repeated the study with a second group and saw the same result.
